parameters.content:
## Notifications

One dispatch point for everything Adericel needs a person to see.

Routing is by severity, not by event type, so an urgent item reaches people the same way regardless of which workflow produced it.

Configure `ADERICEL_NOTIFY_EMAIL` for email or `ADERICEL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL` for a chat webhook. With neither set, messages are recorded in the execution log only — which is a legitimate configuration for a deployment that reads Adericel directly.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Called with { subject, message, severity, organisationId, correlationId }.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Send email
nodes.notes: A failed notification must not fail the operation that produced it. The underlying event is already durably recorded in Adericel.

nodes.name: Recorded in the execution log
nodes.notes: No delivery channel is configured. The message is visible in this execution, and the underlying event is in Adericel regardless.

meta.description: Single notification dispatch point, routing by severity and always carrying the correlation id needed to trace the operation.

parameters.content:
## Error handler

Every Adericel workflow names this as its error workflow.

A failed workflow must leave the system in a **known** state. This handler records what failed, where, and with which correlation id, so the failure can be traced through Adericel rather than being a gap in the record.

It never retries anything: a blind retry of an unknown failure is how one problem becomes two.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

meta.description: Central error workflow. Records what failed with its correlation id and alerts, without retrying anything.

parameters.content:
## Assessment

Asks the Adericel API to assess. **The Truth Engine runs inside Adericel, never here.**

If assessment logic lived in an n8n Code node it would be a second, untested implementation of the truth model, it could not be replayed, and a workflow edit would silently change what the organisation believes to be true. All this workflow does is ask, and report what came back.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Called with { organisationId, correlationId }.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Run full assessment
nodes.notes: Assesses every control, then rolls up requirements, frameworks and the organisation so each level aggregates freshly assessed children.

parameters.errorMessage: =Assessment failed with HTTP {{ $json.statusCode }}. Assurance state has NOT been updated; the previous state remains authoritative.

nodes.name: Assessment failed
nodes.notes: A failed assessment leaves the previous state in place. Adericel never substitutes a guess for a determination it could not make.

meta.description: Requests a full reassessment from the Adericel API and reports the outcome. Contains no assessment logic of its own.

parameters.content:
## Assurance change

Classifies what actually happened, then notifies proportionately.

**Losing visibility is its own event.** A control moving from Proven to Unknown is not a smaller failure — it usually means a source stopped collecting, which is Adericel's problem to fix, not the customer's.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Invoked on AssuranceStateChanged.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Worth notifying?
nodes.notes: Improvements are recorded but do not page anyone. Alert fatigue is how real alerts get ignored.

nodes.name: Recorded only
nodes.notes: The change is already durably recorded in Adericel; no notification is warranted.

meta.description: Classifies an assurance state change, distinguishing a deterioration from a loss of visibility, and notifies proportionately.

parameters.content:
## Finding triage

Decides whether to **propose** a remediation. It never decides whether one runs — the Adericel policy engine does that, and for anything consequential a person does.

The remediation is read from the ruleset that raised the finding, so this workflow contains no mapping of its own between findings and fixes.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Invoked on FindingCreated.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Read available capabilities
nodes.notes: The set of things Adericel can actually execute in this deployment. A remediation with no connector behind it is recorded for a human rather than proposed.

meta.description: Decides whether a finding has an automatable remediation declared by the rule that raised it, and either proposes it or records it for a person.

parameters.content:
## Action proposal

Proposes a remediation. **Nothing is dispatched by this workflow.**

Adericel evaluates policy on the proposal and returns the full decision — which rule matched, the effective autonomy level, how many approvals are needed. If policy denies it, the action ends here and the reason is recorded.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Called with { organisationId, findingId, actionType, targetNodeId, targetExternalId, correlationId }.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Propose to Adericel
nodes.notes: Adericel evaluates policy synchronously and returns the decision. This call proposes; it never executes.

meta.description: Proposes a remediation to Adericel, which evaluates policy and returns the decision. This workflow dispatches nothing itself.

parameters.content:
## Approval

This workflow **cannot approve anything**, by design.

The Adericel API refuses an approval presented by an API key or a workflow, and refuses one from the person who proposed the action. Four-eyes control is meaningless if the system that proposed a change can also authorise it.

All this does is make sure a human knows there is a decision waiting, and give them what they need to make it.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Invoked on ActionApprovalRequested.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Awaiting a person
nodes.notes: The workflow ends here. Approval happens in the Adericel interface, by a person, and is recorded against their identity in the audit trail.

meta.description: Notifies approvers that a decision is waiting, with the full policy decision. Cannot itself approve anything.

parameters.content:
## Action execution

Dispatches an action Adericel has **already authorised**.

The API enforces the state machine: an action that is not AUTHORISED is refused with 412, whatever this workflow asks for. Execution is also exactly-once — the attempt is recorded before dispatch, so an n8n retry finds the prior attempt instead of repeating the change.

**Executed is not successful.** The action moves to VERIFYING and only reaches CONFIRMED once re-observation supports it.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Invoked on ActionApproved, or directly after an autonomous ALLOW.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Execute
nodes.notes: Deliberately NOT retried at the node level. Adericel makes execution exactly-once, and an attempt whose outcome is unknown must be reconciled by a person rather than repeated.

nodes.name: Settle before verifying
nodes.notes: External systems are eventually consistent. Verifying immediately would frequently report INCONCLUSIVE for a change that did in fact take effect.

meta.description: Dispatches an authorised action exactly once, then hands over to verification. Escalates an unknown outcome to a person rather than retrying it.

parameters.content:
## Verification

**An action being issued is not the desired state being achieved.**

Adericel re-collects from the source and compares what it now observes against what the action was supposed to achieve. Three outcomes:

- `CONFIRMED` — re-observation supports it
- `REFUTED` — the change did not take effect; rollback is required
- `INCONCLUSIVE` — cannot tell. The action stays **UNVERIFIED**, and is never reported as successful.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Invoked on VerificationRequested, or after execution.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Verify
nodes.notes: Adericel re-collects from the integration rather than accepting the executor own report. A verification that trusted the execution would prove nothing.

meta.description: Asks Adericel to re-observe the external system and reports honestly when a change cannot be confirmed.

parameters.content:
## Evidence ingestion

Accepts observations from anywhere — a customer script, an MSP platform, another workflow — and pushes them into Adericel.

**n8n does not normalise or assess.** It posts observations to the API, which normalises them deterministically and records provenance. Doing that work here would create a second implementation of the truth model that nobody tests.

nodes.name: Observations in
nodes.notes: Protected by a header credential. Callers present the shared ingestion token; the organisation is taken from the payload and authorised by the Adericel API, never trusted from the caller alone.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Post observations
nodes.notes: Adericel deduplicates observations on content as well, so a repeated batch converges rather than inflating the evidence base.

nodes.name: Respond rejected
nodes.notes: The caller is told the ingest failed and with what status, so it can retry rather than silently losing the batch.

meta.description: Accepts observation batches over an authenticated webhook and forwards them to the Adericel API for normalisation and provenance.

parameters.content:
## Document processing

The **AI/truth boundary** is enforced here.

1. The document is stored as evidence. That is the proof, and it is hash-verified on upload.
2. If AI extraction is enabled, whatever it produces enters as `AI_SUGGESTED` / `CANDIDATE` claims.
3. The Truth Engine **refuses** to consume an unconfirmed AI claim. A person must confirm it, and only a signed-in user can.

An extraction confidence is recorded against the claim. It describes the extraction, never the organisation, and it is never presented as a probability that the organisation is secure.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Called with { organisationId, documentUrl or binary, title, sourceSystem, correlationId }.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Record document as evidence
nodes.notes: Integrity is recorded as UNVERIFIED: Adericel received this document from a workflow and can attest to what it stored, not to the document being genuine.

nodes.name: AI extraction enabled?
nodes.notes: Extraction is off by default. Adericel works completely without it; AI only ever proposes.

nodes.name: Record candidate claim
nodes.notes: The API refuses an AI_SUGGESTED claim created as CONFIRMED. Promotion is a separate, audited decision that only a signed-in person can make.

nodes.name: Stored without extraction
nodes.notes: The document is evidence in its own right. Extraction is an optional convenience, not a requirement for the document to count.

meta.description: Stores a document as evidence and, where enabled, records AI-extracted claims as candidates that cannot influence assurance until a person confirms them.

parameters.content:
## Observation normalisation

For sources that push a vendor-shaped payload. This maps **field names only**.

It deliberately does not decide anything: an absent field stays absent so the control becomes UNKNOWN, rather than being defaulted to a value that would manufacture certainty.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Called with { organisationId, sourceSystem, mapping, records }.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

meta.description: Maps vendor-shaped payloads onto Adericel canonical observations without defaulting absent fields, then submits them through the standard ingestion path.

parameters.content:
## Organisation onboarding

Called on `OrganisationCreated`. Establishes the first assurance picture and reports honestly how much of it is unknown.

A new customer with no sources connected is **not** compliant — it is unknown, and the summary says so in those words.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Invoked by the event intake workflow on OrganisationCreated.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Read organisation
nodes.notes: Confirms provisioning committed before any work is done against the organisation.

nodes.name: Provisioned?
nodes.notes: A partially provisioned organisation would produce assurance states that mean nothing.

nodes.name: Any sources?
nodes.notes: Branches on whether there is anything to collect at all.

nodes.name: Collect from source
nodes.notes: One failing source must not abandon onboarding. The failure is recorded against that integration and its controls report UNKNOWN.

parameters.errorMessage: =Organisation could not be read (HTTP {{ $json.statusCode }}). Onboarding stopped rather than continuing on partial state.

meta.description: Establishes the first assurance picture for a newly created organisation and reports how much of it remains unknown.

parameters.content:
## Scheduled collection

Refreshes evidence across the portfolio.

This is a **safety net**, not the primary schedule — Adericel's worker holds the authoritative schedule in its database, so an n8n outage delays collection rather than losing it. Both paths are idempotent, so running both is harmless.

nodes.name: Every four hours
nodes.notes: Evidence freshness limits are measured in days, so four-hourly collection keeps well inside them.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: MSP configured?
nodes.notes: Set ADERICEL_MSP_ID so this workflow knows which portfolio to sweep.

nodes.name: One organisation at a time
nodes.notes: Sequential rather than parallel. A portfolio sweep that hammered every customer tenant at once would trip their rate limits and look like an attack.

nodes.name: Collect
nodes.notes: A failing source is recorded against that integration and its controls report UNKNOWN. It never stops the rest of the sweep.

parameters.errorMessage: ADERICEL_MSP_ID is not set on this n8n instance, so there is no portfolio to sweep.

meta.description: Sweeps the portfolio and refreshes evidence from every collectable source, one organisation at a time.

parameters.content:
## Scheduled reassessment

Reassesses every organisation.

Reassessment matters even when nothing was collected: evidence expires. A control that was Proven last week becomes **Unknown** once the evidence behind it passes its freshness limit, and that transition is the whole difference between continuous assurance and an annual audit.

nodes.name: Every six hours
nodes.notes: Offset from collection so assessment runs against freshly collected evidence.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

parameters.errorMessage: ADERICEL_MSP_ID is not set on this n8n instance.

meta.description: Reassesses every active organisation so that expiring evidence moves controls into Unknown rather than leaving a stale Proven in place.

parameters.content:
## Evidence expiry

Chases evidence that is about to stop supporting a claim.

This is the highest-leverage operational workflow an MSP runs: chasing evidence a week before it expires prevents a customer silently sliding into Unknown, which is far cheaper than explaining afterwards why the assurance picture went dark.

nodes.name: Daily
nodes.notes: Early enough that a chase lands at the start of the working day.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

parameters.errorMessage: ADERICEL_MSP_ID is not set on this n8n instance.

meta.description: Identifies customers whose evidence position is degrading and chases before controls go Unknown.

parameters.content:
## Portfolio reporting

A weekly portfolio summary for the MSP.

Deliberately contains **no score**. It reports counts with their denominators, and it reports unknowns separately from failures, because those need different responses: a failing control is the customer's problem to fix, an unknown one is usually ours.

nodes.name: Weekly
nodes.notes: Monday morning, so it is read before the week is planned.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

parameters.errorMessage: ADERICEL_MSP_ID is not set on this n8n instance.

meta.description: Weekly portfolio report reporting counts with denominators and keeping unknowns separate from failures.

parameters.content:
## Health monitor

Watches Adericel itself.

The distinction this workflow exists to preserve: **"the customer has an assurance problem" is not the same as "Adericel has an operational problem"**. A failed integration produces Unknown states that look identical to a customer with no controls in place, and only one of those is the customer's fault.

nodes.name: Every 15 minutes
nodes.notes: Frequent enough to catch a stalled worker before a whole assessment cycle is missed.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

meta.description: Watches Adericel's own health and dead-letter queue, distinguishing platform problems from customer assurance problems.

parameters.content:
## Dead-letter recovery

Adericel never drops an event. One that exhausts its delivery attempts lands in a dead-letter queue and stays there.

That matters because a lost `AssuranceStateChanged` means a dashboard is quietly wrong — the worst failure mode for a system whose product is telling the truth.

This workflow surfaces the backlog for a person. It does **not** replay automatically: an event that failed eight times needs diagnosis, not a ninth attempt.

nodes.name: Hourly
nodes.notes: Frequent enough that a backlog is noticed within the hour.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

meta.description: Surfaces undelivered and dead-lettered events for diagnosis rather than replaying them automatically.

parameters.content:
## Offboarding

Drives a customer’s departure to completion.

The order is deliberate and is the opposite of the convenient one: **export first**, then revoke, then close. The moment a customer is least able to argue about their record is exactly when it is most likely to be destroyed, so the export is taken before anything is revoked and closure is refused without one.

This workflow never closes an organisation on its own initiative. It carries out the steps and reports what remains; a person decides that the relationship has ended.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: Called with { organisationId, reason }. Reason is required — an organisation closed without a recorded reason is one nobody can explain later.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Begin offboarding
nodes.notes: Stops collection and assessment immediately. Nothing further is asserted about an estate Adericel no longer observes.

nodes.name: Take the final export
nodes.notes: The record the customer leaves with. Refused by the API if it would be truncated, because a bundle that says it is complete and is not is worse than no bundle.

nodes.name: Revoke everything
nodes.notes: Passport shares stop answering, stored credentials are destroyed rather than disabled, and sessions end. Idempotent, so a partial run is simply repeated.

parameters.errorMessage: Offboarding needs a recorded reason. An organisation closed without one is one nobody can explain to an auditor, a customer or a court.

meta.description: Carries a departing customer through export, revocation and readiness to close, in that order. Never closes an organisation by itself.

parameters.content:
## Sources that disagree

Two integrations contradicting each other is the one failure that looks like success: both are connected, both are healthy, and neither is wrong in a way any error would catch.

Adericel refuses to choose between them, so the affected controls read **Unknown** until somebody settles it. That is the honest answer and it is also invisible unless something goes looking — which is what this does.

nodes.name: Every four hours
nodes.notes: Often enough that a disagreement is noticed the same working day.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

parameters.errorMessage: ADERICEL_MSP_ID is not set on this n8n instance.

meta.description: Finds facts Adericel is withholding because two systems disagree, and names both positions so somebody can settle it.

parameters.content:
## Coverage watch

An integration that loses a permission does not fail. It keeps connecting, keeps returning what it still can, and the controls behind the missing permission quietly become **Unknown** — indistinguishable from a customer who genuinely has no such evidence.

This asks each organisation what its integrations can currently see, and reports any capability that is failing **with the exact permission to grant**. That is the difference between an integration fixed before lunch and one broken for a fortnight.

nodes.name: Every morning
nodes.notes: Early enough that somebody can act on it during the working day.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

parameters.errorMessage: ADERICEL_MSP_ID is not set on this n8n instance.

meta.description: Reports integration capabilities that are failing, with the exact permission that would restore each one, and flags demonstration data in a live tenant.

parameters.content:
## Retention watch

Adericel publishes a retention schedule and enforces it nightly from the same register the schedule is generated from. This checks that the sweep actually ran.

A sweep that has not run in 48 hours means a period that is being promised and not kept. That is a data protection failure whether or not anyone has noticed, and it is silent by nature — no error, no alert, just rows quietly outliving their basis.

nodes.name: Every morning
nodes.notes: After the nightly sweep, early enough to act on a miss the same day.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Did it run?
nodes.notes: Reads the register and the run record together.

nodes.name: Raise it
nodes.notes: Says what is actually wrong, in the terms it will have to be explained in.

nodes.name: Record what it did
nodes.notes: The quiet answer, kept so the schedule is answerable with evidence.

meta.description: Checks that the nightly retention sweep actually ran, and reports what it removed. A declared retention period that is not enforced is a promise being broken silently.

parameters.content:
## Adericel — Event intake

Every Adericel domain event arrives here.

**Security:** the payload is authenticated by an HMAC over `{timestamp}.{rawBody}` using `ADERICEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Deliveries older than five minutes are rejected, so a captured request cannot be replayed.

**Delivery is at-least-once.** Handlers must tolerate duplicates; the event id makes that straightforward.

nodes.name: Adericel event
nodes.notes: Point the Adericel worker at this instance with N8N_BASE_URL and N8N_ENABLED=true. It posts to /webhook/adericel-events.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Resolves configuration from the n8n environment. Nothing in this export contains a URL, a secret or a tenant identifier. Set ADERICEL_API_BASE_URL, ADERICEL_MSP_ID and the notification variables on the n8n container.

nodes.name: Verify signature
nodes.notes: The webhook is public, so the HMAC is the authentication. Nothing downstream runs until this passes.

nodes.name: Route by event type
nodes.notes: Event types with no handler fall through to "other" and are acknowledged. That is a normal state — the event remains durably recorded in Adericel regardless.

nodes.name: Acknowledge
nodes.notes: No handler for this event type; acknowledged as received.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ accepted: true, eventId: $('Verify signature').first().json.id, correlationId: $('Verify signature').first().json.correlationId }) }}

nodes.name: Respond 202
nodes.notes: Acknowledged once the event is accepted and dispatched. Adericel treats a 2xx as delivered and will not retry it.

meta.description: Signed webhook receiving every Adericel domain event, verifying its authenticity and dispatching it to the appropriate handler.
